claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**What is the name of the child (or children) you're enquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I just wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's good to know you have an 8-year-old son named Alex who lives with you in the UK.

Before I can determine your eligibility, I need to gather a bit more information. Let me start with the first key question:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

(This helps me understand your residency and immigration status, which affects Child Benefit eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now, to continue assessing your eligibility for Alex:

**Are you currently working or self-employed in the UK, or are you not in paid work at the moment?**

(This helps me understand your employment situation, which can be relevant to certain aspects of Child Benefit eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently working, yes. I have a job here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's useful context.

Now I have a question about Alex's living situation:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he spend time living with someone else as well (such as another parent or family member)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

I just have a couple more important questions to complete the picture:

**Has Alex ever been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, or is he currently in local authority care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital. He's been there for a few months now, but I still regularly buy things for him and spend money on his needs while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. That does affect the assessment.

To clarify the situation with Alex's hospital stay:

**Has Alex been in hospital for more than 12 weeks continuously, or has he been there for less than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been there for more than 12 weeks - it's been about 15 weeks now actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Before I make my final assessment, let me just confirm one more thing:

**While Alex has been in hospital for these 15 weeks, has he been receiving treatment there the whole time, or has he been discharged and readmitted during this period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been receiving treatment there the whole time - it's been one continuous stay for the 15 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the relevant rules by checking the official guidance:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. I now have all the information I need. Based on the rules and your circumstances, here's my assessment:

According to the guidance on Child Benefit for children in hospital, you would normally lose entitlement after 12 weeks of continuous hospital stay. However, there is an important exception: **if you regularly spend money on the child while they're in hospital, you can continue to receive Child Benefit**.

You've confirmed that you regularly buy things for Alex and spend money on his needs while he's in hospital. This means you fall within the exception to the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The key reason is that while the standard rule is you lose Child Benefit entitlement after 12 weeks in hospital, there's an important exception: if you regularly spend money on the child while they're in hospital, you can continue to receive it. Since you've confirmed you regularly buy things for Alex and spend money on his needs, you fall within this exception.

**Important next step:** If you haven't already done so, you should notify HMRC about Alex's hospital stay. You can do this online, by phone, or by post. This ensures your payments continue without interruption.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?
